what: The full-screen video stage at the top of the page shrinks into a frame 78% of the screen on the first scroll gesture (wheel, down key, swipe) — the clip-path inset narrows over 1.2s power3.inOut (frame ratio 1106:623, phone width 296:494), and during those 1.2 seconds scrolling is locked so the page does not move down. Once shrunk, the lock is released and the body rises over the frame (the stage stays pinned). When back at the top (scrolled past 40px, then within 2px) it locks again and returns to full screen. Progress goes out as --fx-shrink (0~1) and fx:shrink (detail.open) — used to remove the title or to cut the body into the frame shape

options.ratio: Frame width:height, default 1106/623 — as a number like 1.775
options.[data-fx-part=stage]: Clipping stage (required) — holds the video or photo
options.fx:shrink: Event fired when a stream starts or starts reversing (bubbles) — detail.open (true means into the frame)

from.where: /  detail.html .ws__stagewrap (work detail video stage — 78% frame · 1.2s power3.inOut · title characters leave in a wave)

note: While locked, wheel and touch scrolling are blocked (preventDefault) — that is how the original behaves. It lasts 1.2s and is released after that, and it only applies at the top of the page. If you use Lenis, stop window.lenis and start it again
